      "observations": [
        "All 602 owned diff lines across 10 files were read, including both added test tasks, the standalone component test and fixture, styles, template and shared helper comment. The widget observes status, removes the initial tentative selection, selects known response radios and emits a bubbling setEventResponse detail. The original parent only copies status back to the widget and leaves persistence as a TODO; tests check radio/status/event detail, not saved calendar data or a sent reply.",
        "The original parent uses any-attendee count before dereferencing the invited-attendee result. Its tests force organizer identity to match their descriptor. The actual helper can return null; accepted code later guards that result and hides the widget when none is found. This is a later repair, not evidence that the original covers unrelated attendees. Unknown status and pre-connection attribute changes remain untested lifecycle inputs.",
        "Setting missing status or NEEDS-ACTION returns without clearing the previously checked radio. The explicit reset clears it; the standalone test resets before setting NEEDS-ACTION. The CSS hides only the toggle decoration. Native radio/label associations and decorative images remain separate from actual checked-state or live accessibility results.",
        "The changed helper JSDoc says calIAttendee[], while the newly added callers use plain property descriptors and the implementation creates real CalAttendee instances before copying those properties. That test-helper input shape should be described accurately. It is not a production API rule. Added assertions have non-empty expected-behavior messages; the component test contains a double-negative comment despite correct unchecked assertions.",
        "The original click test uses a timer turn before clicking rather than naming a readiness state; no flakiness is established. Accepted code later clones the displayed occurrence and attendee, calls a response callback or transaction, restores the old status on failure and checks dialog identity before applying a successful result. The failure rollback occurs before that reuse guard; no failure-after-reuse execution was performed. These accepted later persistence actions are separate from this initial display-only phase. No Calendar, event-send, keyboard, screen-reader or rendered test ran.",
        "Current reconciliation resolves the original source packet's pending discussion stage. Parent read primary Bug 2014107 current comments 0–2, activity and footer; B reads that retained complete body here. The later regression 2031920 is an unread activity locator, not this original patch's diagnosed outcome.",
        "B reads C3's exact complete D285099 creation-to-close timeline, all 11 submitted inline bodies and both replacement suggestions. Delegated shadow-root change handling and removal of single-case switches are adopted in the original code. The submitted NEEDS_ACTION spelling is a proposal; the actual original guard uses NEEDS-ACTION.",
        "The author rebuts the proposed feedback loop because assigning checked does not emit change, and keeps response status ownership in calendar-dialog.mjs for a future server-failure path. The original handler still only sets widget state and retains the TODO for event persistence. The author adds reset() to uncheck a reused widget before removing status; this source confirms the stated alternative to simple attribute removal.",
        "Reviewer suggestions to remove show() calls do not establish removal: both new original integration tests still call dialog.show(). Their direct checks cover status and selected radio, with organizer identity setup. They do not establish persisted RSVP updates, a failed server response or live accessibility. The later accepted success guard follows the catch rollback, so it is not a general stale-failure guard.",
        "Initial toggle flash/animation concerns, lint failure/fix, acceptance and rebase-related test-failure reports are historical discussion. Later remote completion markers and linked Try runs are not fresh validation or independent proof of the reported failures."
